claims.text: Femtosecond laser ablation deposits energy rapidly.
Rapid energy deposition during femtosecond ablation creates high supersaturation in the plasma plume.
High plume supersaturation favors homogeneous nucleation.
Femtosecond ablation produces narrowly distributed Pt-Pd-Rh-Ru-Ir nanoparticles.
Femtosecond ablation produces uniformly alloyed Pt-Pd-Rh-Ru-Ir nanoparticles.
Nanosecond ablation permits a longer thermal interaction than femtosecond ablation.
The longer thermal interaction during nanosecond ablation enables extended thermal diffusion.
Extended thermal diffusion during nanosecond ablation can cause surface segregation.
Nanoparticle size distribution is governed by ablation dynamics.
Surface alloy homogeneity is governed by ablation dynamics.
Greater alloy uniformity directly enhances catalytic performance.
Femtosecond-ablation nanoparticles will have a narrower particle-size distribution than nanosecond-ablation nanoparticles.
Femtosecond-ablation nanoparticles will have greater alloy-composition homogeneity than nanosecond-ablation nanoparticles.
Femtosecond-ablation nanoparticles will have higher catalytic activity than nanosecond-ablation nanoparticles.
Femtosecond-ablation nanoparticles will have improved catalytic selectivity relative to nanosecond-ablation nanoparticles.
The proposed comparison uses femtosecond pulses shorter than 200 fs and nanosecond pulses of approximately 10 ns at comparable energy densities in deionized water.
Similar catalytic performance from the femtosecond- and nanosecond-ablation samples would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure of the femtosecond sample to show statistically significant improvements in size uniformity, alloy homogeneity, and catalytic performance would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted-outcome field says similar catalytic performance alone would falsify the hypothesis, whereas the formal rule requires absence of statistically significant improvements in size uniformity, alloy homogeneity, and catalytic performance. These are different falsification criteria.
